key_insight: In ALS, higher levels of selected Alzheimer’s-related CSF biomarkers were associated with better functional or memory performance, but did not distinguish ALS from other neurodegenerative conditions.
clinical_relevance: These biomarkers warrant prospective study as exploratory indicators of ALS status and treatment response, not as established diagnostic or treatment-guiding tools.
method: Retrospective analysis of real-world clinical and CSF data from ALS, Alzheimer’s disease, Huntington’s disease, and other disease controls.
Assessed amyloid peptides, tau proteins, neurofilaments, serum markers, and functional and cognitive measures.
Evaluated longitudinal CSF samples over one year in three tofersen-treated ALS patients.
evidence_signal: Aβ40, Aβ42, and pTau181 correlated positively with ALSFRS-R and serum CK-MB; a higher Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio correlated with better memory, while Alzheimer’s-related biomarkers declined during tofersen follow-up.
watch_item: The retrospective associations and three-patient treatment series cannot establish causality or validate biomarkers of therapeutic response; this study concerns ALS, not AI-driven cancer drug discovery.
paper_title: Alzheimer's disease-related cerebrospinal fluid Biomarkers in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: Real-World Associations with Disease Status, Cognition and Tofersen Response
